We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams 

Wayve’s Robot Software group turns new vehicle programs into stable, reliable robot systems. The Platform Integration team works at the boundary between onboard software and vehicle hardware, bringing up new platforms while building reusable components and frameworks that make every future integration faster and more predictable.

As a Software Engineer on the Platform Integration team, you’ll combine hands-on vehicle and bench work with production software development. Your work will directly enable safe, scalable deployment across multiple vehicle programs.

🧠 Your day-to-day 

- Support software bring-up on benches, HiL systems, and vehicles, including work at international test locations.

- Develop and maintain vehicle-facing software components and shared frameworks.

- Diagnose integration issues across software and hardware boundaries and drive them through resolution.

- Identify architectural improvements that reduce bespoke work and improve reuse.

- Build diagnostics, tooling, and metrics for robot-software reliability and performance.

- Produce clear documentation and runbooks for long-term supportability.

- Collaborate with hardware, safety, controls, calibration, and reliability teams.

🧩 What you’ll be working on 

- New vehicle-program bring-up across embedded compute, sensors, networks, and software services.

- Linux-based robotic and automotive systems with multi-process and distributed architectures.

- ROS2 or similar middleware, node development, message interfaces, and system integration.

- Sensor calibration, synchronisation, data validation, and system-level debugging.

- Automotive-grade compute platforms such as NVIDIA DRIVE and Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride.

- Vehicle communication systems including CAN and Automotive Ethernet.

- Shared abstractions and frameworks that improve reliability across programs.

🙌 You should apply if 

- You have strong software-development experience in C++, Python, or Rust.

- You have delivered production-quality software on Linux-based robotic, embedded, or automotive platforms.

- You understand ROS2 or similar robotics middleware and distributed-system integration.

- You have hands-on experience integrating software with vehicle or embedded hardware.

- You can diagnose complex problems using logs, telemetry, on-target tests, and systematic experimentation.

- You understand vehicle sensors, networking, and the practical realities of platform bring-up.

Experience with drive-by-wire systems, CAN tools, shared frameworks, HiL or simulation, functional safety, technical documentation, or observability would be valuable.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve: 

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: 

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process: 

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

- Initial recruiter screen — 25 mins

- Competency Interviews — Programming and technical domain (2 hours)

- Deep-dive technical interviews — Programming, software design, and hiring-manager/team fit (3 hours)

- Final interview — Mission and values alignment (30 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant): 

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

title: Graduate Technology Strategy Analyst, Physical Sciences / Engineering (2027 start)
description:
Introduction 

Are you a recent or soon-to-be graduate in chemistry, physics, engineering or a related field, excited to put your scientific knowledge and curiosity to work on real-world business issues? Are you interested in understanding why some scientific breakthroughs change the world, while other promising technologies struggle to make it into everyday life? Are you fascinated by how things are made, how people use them and how we can shape a more sustainable future? 

Do you enjoy exploring complex questions, making connections between ideas and working with others to find thoughtful, practical solutions? Would you like to help businesses understand not just what technology can do, but how it can make a meaningful difference? 

If so, this could be a great role for you! 

Who we are 

A key part of Cambridge Consultants, our Advisory team works with clients across Consumer, Energy & Industrial, Telecommunications, Biotech, Healthcare and Defence & Security. Our clients range from early start-ups to global organisations, all looking for ways to use emerging technologies to address challenges , create new possibilities and make a positive impact in their markets. 

Our role is to help them navigate uncertainty, explore opportunities and turn promising ideas into practical outcomes. 

We provide research and insights to support important business choices relating to deep tech. This includes go-to-market strategies, investment support , competitor analysis , market insights, technology road-mapping and strategic foresight. The technologies we explore span exciting developments in biotech, quantum sensing and computing, robotics and physical AI, among many others. 

Your role 

This role sits within the Research & Insights section of our Advisory group. We explore how emerging technologies and future trends might shape the choices businesses make today, helping our clients feel better equipped to navigate change and plan for the future. 

You might investigate what people will value in the next generation of products, explore how cleantech can be adopted at scale, or uncover where novel sensors could create new possibilities for businesses and their customers. 

It's an opportunity to combine scientific thinking, creative exploration and commercial understanding to help answer questions that don't always have straightforward answers. 

What you will be doing 

With guidance and support from our wider Advisory team, you will: 

- 
Explore a variety of meaningful projects spanning climate tech investment, new energy generation, smart mobility strategy and emerging deep tech fields such as quantum. 

- 
Bring fresh perspectives to complex challenges , drawing on different research approaches and ideas to help clients identify opportunities across products, services and operations, including AI-enabled approaches. 

- 
Work collaboratively with specialists in engineering, science, product design and realisation, and business to develop strategies that create commercial and societal benefits. 

- 
Make sense of complex information , analysing markets, technologies and business models to help clients understand their options, consider potential challenges and drive informed actions. 

- 
Share ideas and contribute to thought leadership on how deep tech could help address global challenges , from communication on the moon to the future of repairable consumer devices. 

What you can bring 

We are looking for applicants with the following traits and skills: 

- 
A relevant academic background: A Master's or PhD in physical sciences, maths, data science, engineering or another related discipline. 

- 
Business and commercial thinking: Experience or an interest in entrepreneurship, business or economics, whether through student business plan competitions, internships, start-ups or relevant modules and further study. 

- 
Thoughtful analytical and creative thinking: The ability to explore complex technical ideas, recognise connections and turn findings into clear, practical recommendations. 

- 
Curiosity and adaptability: Enthusiasm for learning about new technologies, exploring different sectors and approaching unfamiliar challenges with an open mind. 

- 
Communication and collaboration: The ability to explain complex ideas clearly, listen to different perspectives and build constructive relationships with people from a range of technical and professional backgrounds. 

How to apply 

If this opportunity interests you, please send your CV and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience, interests and what excites you about the role. 

We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. You don't need to meet every requirement to be a strong candidate. If the role sparks your curiosity and you'd enjoy exploring how science and technology can make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

You understand that any false statement, misleading information, or material omission may render you liable to disqualification from the recruitment process, withdrawal of any offer of employment, or dismissal without notice if discovered following appointment. title: Technical Product Manager, Developer Experience & Product-Led Growth
description:
About Telnyx 

Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network , to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications. 

We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team. 

Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers. 

The Role 

We're looking for a highly technical Product Manager to own how developers discover, build on and grow with Telnyx.

Telnyx operates a global infrastructure platform spanning communications, AI inference, GPUs, edge compute, databases and real-time applications. We've invested heavily in building the underlying infrastructure. Now we want to make it dramatically easier for developers to understand what's possible, build useful applications and get into production.

This is a hands-on product role leading a small team of six engineers across Developer Relations and Product-Led Growth. We aren't looking for a traditional DevRel leader or someone whose primary skill is managing people. We want a strong engineer with excellent product judgment who understands developer experience, builds things personally and knows how to turn developer adoption into revenue. 

The Team 

You'll lead a team of six: three DevRel engineers (sample apps, open source, technical content and demos) and three PLG engineers (activation, AI agents and automation, self-service conversion and expansion). You'll report to the Chief Operating Officer. 

What you'll own 

- Build applications developers actually want to use — Lead the DevRel team in building production-quality sample applications, integrations, templates and reference implementations on Telnyx. Publish them on GitHub, maintain them and make them easy for developers to deploy and extend. Turn those applications into compelling technical content, live demos and developer distribution.

- Drive product-led growth — Own the PLG operation responsible for moving developers from signup to meaningful usage and revenue. Use product telemetry, behavioral signals, AI agents and human intervention to identify friction, accelerate onboarding, improve conversion and expand self-service usage.

- Make the developer experience better — Get hands-on with our APIs, SDKs, documentation and infrastructure. Work directly with product engineering to identify and resolve the issues that make products difficult to use. Our reference applications should continuously test whether our products are genuinely ready for developers.

- Build AI-native growth systems — Work with Growth Engineering and RevOps to develop automated workflows for developer acquisition, onboarding, account intelligence, technical assistance and expansion. We believe small teams of excellent technical people supervising powerful automation can outperform much larger traditional GTM organizations.

- Connect the entire developer journey — Applications attract developers. Developers experiment with the platform. PLG helps them succeed. Production usage generates revenue. The feedback from that process improves our products and informs what we build next. You'll be accountable for making that system work. .

What we're looking for 

- A strong software engineering background. You should be comfortable building and debugging real applications, working with APIs, reading code and understanding complex infrastructure.

- Experience as a Technical Product Manager, founding engineer, technical founder or similar role with substantial personal responsibility for shipping software.

- Exceptional product judgment, particularly around developer tools, APIs, documentation, onboarding and usability.

- Familiarity with AI infrastructure, LLMs, inference, cloud platforms, real-time systems or developer infrastructure.

- Understanding of product-led growth, including developer acquisition, activation, conversion, retention and monetization.

- Ability to work with AI coding agents, automation frameworks, product analytics and modern developer tooling.

- Strong technical communication skills. You can explain complicated technologies clearly and recognize what makes a useful demonstration or reference application.

- Comfortable leading a small technical team while remaining deeply involved in the actual work.

Experience at a developer infrastructure company is valuable. Experience personally building and growing something developers love is more important.

How we'll measure success 

Your primary objective is growing developer-led revenue on Telnyx. 

We'll look at activated developers, production applications deployed, self-service conversion, usage expansion and retention. We'll also measure the adoption of our reference applications, how effectively our developer content attracts users and how quickly developers can get from signup to a working application.

We care about applications developers actually use, not demos shipped for the sake of demos. We care about developers reaching production, not just generating signups. And we care about revenue, not vanity metrics.

Who will thrive here 

Someone who would rather build a working prototype than spend a week debating a roadmap. Someone who notices a broken onboarding experience and immediately starts fixing it. Someone who understands both what makes infrastructure technically excellent and what makes developers want to use it.

You should be capable of leading six very technical people because you have the engineering ability, product instincts and judgment to make everyone around you more effective.

This is a builder's job, not a professional management job. 

We're looking for someone who can make Telnyx a platform developers genuinely love building on, and turn that into a meaningful business.

- Maintain strong broker advocacy by being visible, responsive and passionate about Flock’s product, proposition and mission.

- Use AI in your day-to-day work, from broker research and meeting prep to analysing your pipeline, so your time goes on relationships rather than admin.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK: 

ESSENTIAL 

- A minimum of 5 years of experience in managing broker relationships within the insurance sector, possessing a reputable standing in the industry.

- Energy and innovation in abundance - the ability to work fast, spot opportunity and solve problems. 

- A proven track record of exceeding revenue targets, driving business growth, and closely collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve collective objectives.

- An existing network of broker contacts that will enable a rapid integration and immediate impact within Flock’s business development realm.

- Exceptional understanding of the commercial broker marketplace, competitor carriers, broker business models, and processes.

- Ability to deliver a consultative sales process, aligning Flock’s value proposition with brokers’ current and future business needs.

- Comfortable using AI in your daily work, from research and meeting prep to account analysis, and curious about where else it could help you win business.

PREFERABLE 

- Experience building networks of brokers in a Commercial Motor Fleet setting. 

- Have a broker distribution background with an active panel of brokers in the commercial insurance market. 

- Can embrace new technologies and products, with experience of successfully distributing these to brokers.

WHAT WE OFFER (in addition to a competitive salary) 

- 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖 

- Share Incentive Plan 📈

- Workplace Pension 💰

- £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

- 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

title: Brand Marketing Lead
description:
About Pleo 

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role 

We're looking for a Brand Marketing Lead to join our Brand & Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help own our brand marketing strategy and campaign execution across six European markets and be part of our marketing team as we scale our spend management platform. If you're excited about building category-defining campaigns that move Pleo from a good solution to the undisputed choice for mid-market finance leaders and are passionate about brand strategy and creative execution, then this is the opportunity for you!

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to 

You’ll report to the Director of Integrated Marketing, and work in close collaboration with the Director of Brand Experience and Strategy, as well as the Brand Intelligence Manager, our brand foundations team, PR, content marketing and digital channels team. You’ll partner cross-functionally with PMM, MOPS, CX and sales. This is a hands-on, IC role, where you'll do both the thinking and the work—strategy and execution both sit with you.

What you’ll be doing 

As a Brand Marketing Lead, you will:

- Own the brand marketing strategy that moves Pleo from ‘one of many’ to the undisputed choice for mid-market European finance leaders.

- Build and execute integrated brand campaigns from concept through to reporting — learning from what we’ve just launched, and pushing further.

- Create branded content that shows how financial services should be done. Content that recognizes the precision, rigor, and craft that finance leaders bring to their work.

- Manage the funnel strategically — balancing awareness, consideration, and conversion. Not just fishing in the pond of people who already know us, but earning the right to speak to people we don’t know yet.

- Own your budget and agency relationships — you’re the strategic partner they answer to.

- Measure what matters — working with Brand Intelligence, Integrated Marketing, Data, and MOps to track brand lift, earned media, consideration, and how brand work flows into pipeline and revenue.

- Set the benchmark for brand work in fintech — prove that category-defining campaigns come from strategic rigor and creative excellence working together. You’ll establish Pleo as the model for how brands should think about their audience, and show that understanding someone better than anyone else is a more powerful differentiator than any feature.

What you bring 

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

- 10+ years in brand marketing (B2B or fintech might be helpful, but we care more about the thinking than the category)

- A portfolio of work that shows you’ve led campaigns from strategy through to execution — ideally integrated campaigns that work across multiple channels

- Strong stakeholder management skills — you can influence a room, sell an idea, and push back when something isn’t working

- Strategic thinking + execution mindset — you’re equally comfortable building a 6-month brand strategy and getting your hands dirty on day-to-day campaign work

- Comfort with ambiguity and pace — this is a growing company, and things move fast. You thrive in that

- Understanding of how brand and pipeline connect — you know that brand campaigns need to serve business growth, not just awareness

- A point of view on category dynamics — you can look at a market and spot where everyone’s getting it wrong

- A strong understanding for when/how to localise concepts, messaging & GTM campaigns across different markets.

- Fluency in one or more of our European markets is a bonus (not required, but helpful)

Why is this role a good fit for you 

This role is a good fit for you if:

- You want to reframe an entire category's conversation by competing on human insight rather than just feature parity.

- You thrive in a fast-paced, autonomous environment where you can build campaigns that serve as a 5-year foundation.

- You believe brand strategy must be grounded in audience understanding and directly drive business outcomes.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

- You prefer purely high-level strategy without getting hands-on with day-to-day campaign execution.

- You operate best in rigid, highly structured environments with slow moving pace and minimal ambiguity.

- You view brand marketing in isolation from performance data, pipeline metrics, and commercial growth.

How you’ll develop in this role 

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

- Map customer journeys across SMB, mid-market, and enterprise segments to identify brand opportunities.

- Develop a comprehensive European brand roadmap that builds on recent launch momentum.

- Develop a comprehensive European brand roadmap that builds on recent launch momentum.

The location 

Please note: We can hire on a hybrid set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work . We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.

Show me the benefits! 

- Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

- Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

- Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

- 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

- For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

- We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

- Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process 

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

- Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

- Hiring Manager Interview: A 45 minute chat to deep dive into your experience

- Challenge & Team Interview: We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role

- Final Interview : A final interview with a senior leader

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for this role, we received a total vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

- CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

- Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

- Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

About your application 

- English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

- A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

- Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

- Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email ----- We’ll design a process that works for you.

- Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here .

- Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

- Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

title: VP of Data
description:
About Us 

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem .

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

Why this role, why now 

12,000+ companies trust Perk with their travel and spend, and we've brought both together in one intelligent platform. Every booking, expense and invoice adds to a wealth of data at your fingertips, and now is the moment to enable teams to use this data intelligently to power better decisions, precise reporting, and to create cost and time savings for our customers. Come lead the team that makes all of this possible.

The Role 

Data is at the core of Perk's innovation and the backbone of how we will evolve our products using new technology. As our VP of Data, you'll step into one of the most influential leadership roles in Builders (Data, Product, Design, Engineering) with a direct hand in shaping Perk's strategy and success, and we scale our multi product platform.

Reporting to our President of Product and Technology, you'll lead a 40+ person organisation, with a remit that spans our Travel, Spend, and Events products. This role also spans our core functions and drives the business, including Customer Care, Marketing, Finance, Revenue and People. You'll join a strong, talented team with a clear mandate to shape how we create exceptional products at Perk, using our proprietary data.

Across travel, spend, and events, Perk holds a wealth of data that touches every booking, expense, invoice and payment. Your opportunity is to reshape it so it powers smarter, more intelligent products that keep us on the cutting edge of what is possible.

This is a role for a data leader who thrives in fast-paced environments, scales high-performing organisations through senior leaders, and has the technical credibility to go deep when it matters. You'll join a top-notch leadership team where we elevate each other, build shared strategies and win together. You'll help define how we grow and make decisions, with accountability for data across the whole company.

Your team 

You’ll lead a talented, collaborative and innovative team who are excellent at what they do. They span seven crafts: Data Product Partners, Reporting Analytics, Data Analytics, Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, Data Science and Data Governance. Together they power the work the business relies on every day, and they’re ready to take data to its next stage of scale with you.

Your missions 

- Strategy and Roadmap . More than ever data informs everything we do and is core to the AI native products that we build. You’ll own the long term vision and strategy for data architecture, analytics, predictive modeling, and AI product integration . Work hand in hand with Product, Engineering and Platform teams across Perk to turn machine learning and advanced analytics into products customers love.

- Set the standard for trust. Own data governance, privacy and compliance, so security and regulatory requirements are built in from the start. Partner with our AI leadership to make sure the data behind every AI product is trusted, so everything we build earns customer confidence.

- Build a data platform we rely on. Run data infrastructure like a flagship product: governed, reliable, built for scale from day one. You own the budget and the build, buy and prioritisation calls.

- Lead with conviction. Unify the craft, standards and roadmap across teams so data speaks with one voice, and anticipates questions before they're asked. Be the data voice alongside Product, Engineering, Finance, Customer Care, Marketing, Revenue and People.

- Grow leaders who grow the business. Coach your senior leaders, shape the operating model and org design, attract top talent, and build a culture of ownership, autonomy and measurable results.

What success looks like 

- Data is the foundation of products that know our customers and anticipate what they need: personalised experiences, smarter recommendations and proactive insights, so they get answers before they have to ask.

- You've built a high-performing, trusted data organisation that delivers measurable value across the business so all functions use and trust the data to shape decisions, inform strategy and change how we work, well beyond reporting.

- Your teams operate with clear priorities, solid infrastructure and real ownership, and what they ship is core to our business and our success.

- Lead and influence, partner with executive leaders to shape the questions and drive the decisions that matter most.

What you'll bring 

- Proven scale-up leadership. You've led data organisations in high-growth tech or SaaS, and you've built this muscle before.

- Leader of leaders. You've scaled organisations of 40 or more through senior leaders, coached leaders of leaders and hired top talent.

- Technical excellence and innovation. A data science background combined with analytics and data engineering, and the depth to push what's possible in any direction.

- Executive leadership. You've owned a data strategy and budget at executive level, made the big build, buy and invest calls, and helped set company direction alongside senior leadership.

- Modern stack fluency. Fluency across the modern data stack, such as dbt, Snowflake, conversational analytics and Looker or Tableau, plus the instinct to build your own tooling where it gives us an edge.

- Trust by design. Deep understanding of data privacy, governance and compliance, including GDPR.

- Partnership at every level. Proven trusted partnerships across Product, Engineering, Finance and Operations, and the communication skills to influence at the most senior levels and drive alignment.

- Big picture and fine detail. You move comfortably between company-level strategy and hands-on specifics.

AI at Perk 
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work 

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

- Own the technical architecture of our CRM, Attio. Shape its data model, objects, workflows and integrations. You’ll be hands-on with configuration, particularly early on, but routine admin won’t be the sole focus of the role.

- Build and maintain integrations. Make data flow reliably across Attio and our wider toolset, including Apollo, Cal.com , Tally and Polytomic, and into the data systems used by the wider business.

- Own the wider toolset. Assess new tools and vendors, improve or replace what isn’t working, and make sure the stack is useful, reliable and cost-conscious.

- Find opportunities for automation and AI. Identify work that could be made easier for Sales and CS, and build or collaborate on solutions where they fit the priorities of the stack.

- Keep systems dependable. Troubleshoot problems, establish sensible governance and documentation, and partner with IT on access and security.

- Understand how teams work. Get close to Sales and CS workflows so the systems you build solve real problems, not just technical ones.

What We’re Looking For 

- Experience designing, building and owning systems used by a growing commercial team. Relevant hands-on experience matters more to us than a particular number of years or experience with a specific CRM.

- Curiosity about AI-powered GTM workflows, with experience building them a plus rather than a prerequisite.

- A collaborative, low-ego approach. You can work through messy requests with Sales, CS and Data, challenge assumptions constructively, and ship solutions people can use.

- You don’t need to have used Attio or every tool in our stack. We’re more interested in what you’ve built, how you think about systems, and how you’d apply that experience here.

We are living in the most exciting time for tool builders since Engelbart's demo in 1968 and we want to assemble the best crew to build this future together. Our compensation philosophy is to hire the best people in the market and pay them accordingly with salary, variable, and equity.

- That's the problem we're solving. Cytix helps organisations understand which software changes actually matter, what should happen next, and how to prove the right call was made. Security understood, in other words.

We're a small team with big plans, so every person we hire genuinely shapes what Cytix becomes. Make the first move. When the goal is clear but the path isn't, you get moving rather than waiting for perfect instructions. If you're blocked, you make a sensible call, say what you're assuming, and explain how you'd course-correct. We'd rather you act and be slightly wrong than sit still.

Find the smarter path. You ask why before how. You dig into what the real problem is instead of just building what the spec says, and you're happy to question 'that's how it's always been done' when the reason behind it has gone stale.

See it through. When something's yours, it lands. No loose ends, no surprises for whoever picks it up next. You keep people posted when things change, and if something falls between roles, you catch it.

Raise the bar. You do the best job possible in the time you've got, whether that's a day or a month. Sometimes that means deep craft; sometimes the smartest move is quick and scrappy. It's about good judgement, and we hold each other to it without blame or politics.

Play to win. You care about the mission but don't take yourself too seriously. You say 'I' when things go wrong and 'we' when they go right, trust teammates to do things their own way, and bring a bit of humour when the pressure's on.

Samsara sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world, processing 25+ trillion data points annually across thousands of connected devices. In this role, you will: 

- Lead the ongoing strategy, operation, and continuous improvement of Samsara's vulnerability management program, along with other core application security programs — not just execute against an existing process, but define what the process should be.

- Own and drive down mean time to remediate (MTTR) across the vulnerability backlog, as SLAs tighten.

- Build and champion automation and tooling that scale vulnerability detection and response across cloud, firmware/IoT, and corporate systems, rather than relying on manual, one-by-one review.

- Set technical and architectural direction for the program, translating leadership's strategic priorities into a concrete execution plan for the team.

- Communicate risk and remediation tradeoffs to engineering leadership in terms they can act on, without owning the relationship end to end.

- Participate in security incident investigations involving high-profile vulnerabilities, assessing potential impact on Samsara's infrastructure.

- Be regularly on call to support critical vulnerability response.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices 

Minimum requirements for the role: 

- 10+ years of relevant experience as a cloud engineer or security engineer, including hands-on vulnerability management across a broad, multi-product enterprise environment — not a single product or team's slice of it.

- Proficiency in Go, Python, and JavaScript.

- Demonstrated ability to independently set technical and architectural direction for a security program, and to drive remediation across a broad, multi-surface environment without direct authority over the teams doing the fixing.

- Significant experience with modern vulnerability management tooling (e.g., Wiz, Semgrep) and deep familiarity with vulnerability scoring frameworks such as CVSS and EPSS.

- Strong AWS cloud services background.

- Deep understanding of Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and Software Composition Analysis (SCA).

- Hands-on use of AI/LLM tooling in your own security workflow — triage, detection logic, remediation drafting — plus credibility speaking to how AI is changing the threat landscape and the tooling available to address it.

- Location: must be based in central or eastern timezones.

- Experience with C/C++, relevant to firmware and embedded systems.

- Background at a cloud-native, AI-forward company actively building agentic or AI-driven products.

- Experience with security automation platforms (e.g., Tines) and serverless frameworks (e.g., AWS Lambda).

- Experience integrating vulnerability management into modern CI/CD pipelines with a "shift-left" mentality.

- Experience spanning SaaS, firmware, and corporate IT security programs — not just one product line.

- Experience managing vulnerabilities within a FedRAMP-certified environment.

- Experience building, extending, or wiring up AI copilots/agents for security workflows (e.g., automated triage, remediation drafting).

Total Rewards 

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable. 

Belonging at Samsara

This is a demanding, high-ownership role. Deadlines do not move, the stakes are real, and the team will rely on you to hold the line. We are looking for someone who wants that responsibility.

Bid Management - from first read to submission 

- Screen and qualify opportunities with your sales director; prepare bid/no-bid decisions with risks, resources, and price on the table

- Break each tender down (NATO IFB or RFQ, EU call, RFP for a Nation through EU-NATO platforms such as NSPA or SAFE joint procurement) into a compliance matrix, a bid plan and clear owners

- Write and assemble the management, technical and compliance volumes with Engineering, Product, Finance and Legal

- Organise the review gates and prepare the final price review with Finance; submit complete, compliant and on time, every time

- Run the clarification rounds and support your sales director in negotiations through to contract signature

NATO & EU Procurement - the rules of the game 

- Master NSPA and NCIA procedures: Source File registration, declarations of eligibility, notifications of intent, IFBs and RFQs, basic ordering agreements and framework contracts

- Run EU grant proposals (European Defence Fund, EDIP): Funding & Tenders portal, consortium building, Part A and Part B, lump-sum budgets

- Track national procurement rules and partners on the Eastern Flank through EU-NATO (Poland, Romania, the Baltic States…), e.g. via NSPA or SAFE joint procurement

- Build and maintain the bid library: company documents, CVs, past performance, standard answers, templates

Project Delivery - from award to acceptance 

- Turn each award into a project: kick-off, plan, milestones, risks, budget and change control

- Coordinate engineering, production, demo and logistics teams, and partners, to deliver what we promised when we promised it

- Own customer reporting, deliverables and acceptance (FAT/SAT), with the documentation trail for invoicing and audits

- Run several projects in parallel, each at a different stage

Process & Reporting 

- Set the bid and project rhythm for the team: calendar, gates, templates, dashboards

- Review the status of every live bid and project weekly with your sales director: deadlines, compliance, risks, resources needed

- Run lessons learned after every bid, won or lost

Candidate Profile 

- 5+ years in bid, proposal or project management in defence, aerospace or security

- Proven record of compliant, on-time submissions to NATO agencies, EU programmes or European ministries of defence, several of them in parallel

- At least one defence contract delivered from award to acceptance

- Scale-up or lean-team experience is a significant advantage; prime experience is welcome if you want more breadth and speed

Skills & Qualities 

- Rigorous and precise compliance is binary; in defence, the margin for error is zero

- Built for parallel work you run several bids and projects at once, prioritise hard and never drop the ball

- Committed you own the outcome, not just your part of it; submission peaks are part of the job and you plan for them

- Calm under pressure fixed deadlines, late amendments and competing requests do not throw you

- A clear writer structured, scoreable English; you turn engineering input into compliant answers

- A leader without authority you get engineers, Finance, Legal and partners to deliver on time

- Technically curious you understand how sensors, effectors, C2 and AI fit together, or you learn it fast

- Discreet and trustworthy you handle sensitive commercial and defence information as a matter of course

- Mission-driven you care about European security, not just the job title

Nice to Have 

- APMP, Shipley, PMP, PRINCE2 or IPMA certification

- Experience on a European Defence Fund or EDIP consortium, or with NSPA/NCIA procurement

- A background in a NATO agency, the EDA or a ministry of defence, or military service (officer or NCO)

- Knowledge of C-UAS, air defence, ISR or drones

- Export-control experience (French export licensing, EU dual-use rules)

Security 

- This position will require applying for a NATO personnel security clearance; it is therefore open to nationals of EU Member States that are also NATO members, and the hire is subject to the clearance procedure

Languages 

- Professional English, written and spoken (C1) is mandatory

- French is a strong plus

- Polish, Romanian, Lithuanian or Ukrainian is a plus

Travel 

- Regular travel to NATO agencies (Brussels, Luxembourg, The Hague), EU institutions, and to demos and acceptance tests across Europe

Everyone in Growth works in Claude Code with a shared library of skills and connectors, a common repository that holds our workflow spec, our decision log and our merchant context, and a simple delivery lifecycle (Research → Spec → Plan → Build) where each stage ends with a human decision. Claude does the legwork; a person decides. Correctness comes from automated verification (tests, adversarial agent review, live validation), and every production change goes through a pull request with a named reviewer from DevX or SRE.

We are rebuilding our GTM system around five layers: market definition, signals, data & enrichment, decision & routing, and activation. As part of it, we are moving our merchant lifecycle off HubSpot to a modern customer engagement platform. Braze leads, Customer.io is in the running, and we want your view. You will lead that migration and the lifecycle programme built on top of it.

You will join a team of 6 with a Growth Ops, a Growth Engineer, a Paid Acquisition Manager, a Senior GTM Engineer (hiring) and an Experimentation & Tracking Engineer (hiring), and you will report to Julian, Team Lead Growth.

This position is a permanent contract (CDI) based in Paris, hybrid. 

💼 About the job

Own the B2B lifecycle, from lead to active merchant 

- Design and run the journeys that drive revenue: lead nurturing, onboarding, activating signed merchants who haven't taken a first payment, retention and win-back.

- Reach the right merchants at the right moment with the right message, using segments built on live data (industry, size, country, TPV, product usage).

- Alma is opening up to B2C, with new consumer products on the way. You'll be the first lifecycle person to work on it, and you'll get to invent how Alma talks to consumers.

- It starts small next to the merchant work and is set to grow fast.

Lead the migration off HubSpot 

- Help pick the platform. Braze is the front-runner, and if you think Customer.io or another tool fits better, make the case.

- Audit what runs today, decide what to rebuild, improve or drop, and plan the switch so no key communication stops along the way.

- With the Growth Engineer and Data, define the data model, consent management and deliverability setup, then switch off HubSpot marketing on schedule.

Measure what you ship 

- Use control groups and A/B tests by default. Report on activations, reactivations and influenced TPV rather than open rates.

- Build your own segments and analyses, and share what works with Sales, Account Management and Revenue Marketing.

Be the CRM project lead across Revenue 

- Align Sales, Account Management, Ops, Product Marketing, Brand and Legal on shared campaigns: you own the brief-to-delivery workflow, set the pace and arbitrate.

- Make other teams autonomous on simple communications (templates, tone of voice, golden rules), so you can focus on the programmes that move revenue.

🗓️ Your first months

- Months 1–3: you audit our current lifecycle (HubSpot workflows, onboarding emails, scattered tools), give your recommendation on the target platform and define its setup with the Growth Engineer, and keep priority campaigns running while you prepare the switch.

- By month 6: onboarding, activation and retention journeys run on the new platform with control groups; HubSpot marketing is switched off; a yearly campaign calendar is shared with Sales, Account Management and Product Marketing.

🧰 You will work with

- Lifecycle: Braze, Customer.io or equivalent (decision in progress). HubSpot until we switch it off.

- Revenue systems & data: Salesforce (system of record), BigQuery, Looker

- AI & delivery: Claude Code (skills, connectors), Notion, Linear

🧩 About you

To succeed in this job 

- 5+ years in lifecycle, CRM or marketing automation, across both B2B and B2C. On the B2B side, you have run programmes hand in hand with Sales or Account Management on large portfolios (1,000+ accounts). On the B2C side, you have built consumer activation and engagement journeys at scale.

- A campaign manager first: you turn a business goal into a segment, a timing and a message, and you can show the revenue impact of your past programmes.

You build journeys, segments and personalisation yourself, and you have opinions on what each tool does well and where it falls short. Having led or contributed to a platform migration is a strong asset.

- Data autonomy: you pull your own segments and results from a BI tool (Looker or equivalent), design tests with control groups, and understand how data flows between a CRM, a warehouse and a marketing platform.

- Cross-functional leadership: you have owned projects involving several teams without formal authority, and you know how to prioritise when everyone needs your time.

description:
Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ?

Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients.

À propos de Pennylane 

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

En 5 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

💰 Lever un total de 350 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1000 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches!

🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible

🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours 

🚀 Déjà plus de 1 000,000 TPE/PME et plus de 6000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !

Localisation et déplacements 

Poste basé à Paris , selon la politique hybride de Pennylane, avec des déplacements réguliers en France auprès des partenaires, de leurs équipes et lors d’événements professionnels. Le portefeuille pourra inclure des partenaires franciliens et nationaux ; son allocation définitive sera précisée avec le manager.

Pourquoi ce rôle est-il important chez nous ?

Les intégrateurs historiques disposent souvent d’une expertise métier reconnue, d’équipes commerciales et de conseil, ainsi que d’un parc de clients à accompagner. Ils peuvent contribuer fortement à la croissance de Pennylane, à la fois par la vente de nouvelles solutions et par le développement de leur parc existant.

Pour transformer ce potentiel en résultats, il faut installer une dynamique commerciale durable : aligner les dirigeants et les équipes terrain, faire émerger des opportunités, améliorer la maîtrise du produit et faciliter la collaboration avec les équipes Pennylane. Tu aideras les partenaires à passer d’une relation de distribution ou de prescription à une collaboration active, structurée et créatrice de valeur.

Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ? 

Tu piloteras le développement d’un portefeuille de partenaires intégrateurs, de la stratégie de compte jusqu’à l’exécution des plans d’action :

- Développer les comptes partenaires , en alignant les dirigeants, responsables commerciaux et équipes opérationnelles autour d’objectifs communs.

- Accélérer le business Resell et Cosell , en animant les opportunités, en améliorant leur qualité et en aidant les partenaires à faire progresser leurs cycles de vente.

- Faire monter les équipes partenaires en compétence , grâce à des démonstrations, des formations et un accompagnement commercial concret.

- Créer une dynamique de croissance sur le parc existant , en identifiant les opportunités de déploiement, de migration et d’équipement des clients des intégrateurs.

- Faire rayonner les apprentissages du terrain , en partageant les résultats, les besoins partenaires et les leviers qui fonctionnent avec l’équipe Partnerships et les autres équipes internes.

Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ? 

1. Construire et déployer les plans de croissance des partenaires

- Comprendre le modèle économique, l’organisation, les priorités et le potentiel de chaque intégrateur.

- Construire avec les dirigeants et responsables commerciaux des plans de compte ambitieux, assortis d’objectifs et d’étapes concrètes.

- Identifier les leviers de croissance adaptés à chaque partenaire : développement du parc, nouveaux projets, campagnes ciblées, événements ou actions conjointes.

- Mobiliser les sponsors et les équipes terrain pour ancrer le partenariat dans les pratiques commerciales et opérationnelles.

- Prioriser ton temps et les ressources internes en fonction du potentiel et de l’impact attendu.

2. Animer le business Resell et Cosell

- Créer et entretenir une relation de confiance avec les décideurs, les équipes commerciales et les consultants du partenaire.

- Suivre le pipeline Resell et Cosell, assurer la qualité des opportunités et rendre le forecast fiable.

- Aider le partenaire à qualifier les besoins, structurer les opportunités et mobiliser les bons interlocuteurs Pennylane.

- Coordonner les actions avec les Account Executives et clarifier les rôles sur les cycles de vente partagés.

- Détecter les risques, débloquer les situations et accélérer les opportunités pertinentes jusqu’à leur conclusion.

3. Développer le parc et les opportunités chez les clients des intégrateurs

- Identifier avec le partenaire les segments de clients et les cas d’usage prioritaires.

title: Solution Consultant, Connect EMEA
description:

title: Stage Marketing B2B
description:

Alexis Soulopoulos [CEO]

As a Security Engineer , you will take ownership of protecting our product, our users, and our collaborators as we scale a fast-growing AI companionship platform. You'll work hands-on across application security, risk & compliance, and security awareness (plus keeping an eye on AI-specific threats as our product line evolves). Given the nature of our product (AI-generated content, including NSFW) you'll play a key role in keeping both our systems and our users safe, with real ownership from day one.

This is a hands-on role reporting directly to the Security Lead, with regular check-ins on priorities.

Key Responsibilities 

Application Security

- Perform weekly code reviews to catch vulnerabilities before they ship

- Track, prioritize, and drive remediation of security vulnerabilities across the stack

- Coordinate external security audits and penetration tests , and follow through on findings

Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC)

- Maintain and evolve our risk register , mapping all company services and prioritizing what's exposed

- Support audit follow-up and keep GRC documentation up to date

Security Awareness

- Communicate new threats to the team , document findings, and broadcast security updates company-wide

- Run phishing simulations and security training (via Riot)

Monitoring & Coverage

- Own the monitoring of security channels and alerts , including weekend coverage, so nothing goes unanswered

IT & Access Management

- Set up and secure new employee devices (MDM), manage access provisioning/deprovisioning

AI Security Monitoring

- Keep an eye on emerging attack techniques targeting generative AI (prompt injection, jailbreaks, content filter bypass)

- Track security incidents and vulnerabilities disclosed by the third-party AI providers we rely on

Your Qualifications

Hard Skills

- Solid experience in application security (code review, vulnerability management)

- Experience coordinating or conducting penetration tests / security audits 

- Comfortable shipping code and working with Git/GitHub workflows

- Scripting/automation skills 

- Bonus: familiarity with AI/LLM security concepts (prompt injection, jailbreaking, adversarial testing) — this is still an emerging field, so curiosity matters more than proven experience

Soft Skills 

🗣 Strong communication & collaborative skills (perfectly fluent in English)

🧢 Goal-orientated, ownership and commitment

⚡️ Doer mindset - we are moving fast and we need people who can find the right balance between executing, planning and strategy

🧢 Humble - willing to learn, open to feedback

🍭 #NSFW - you are comfortable working in an environment with products that are based on uncensored models and content

Why EverAI?

📈 Exponential Growth : From 50M users in 2 years, to 100M next — and 500M beyond

title: Post-doctorant(e) :  Problèmes publics des centres de données - Chaire SHS TerrAINs  - CDD de 18 mois
description:
Qui sommes-nous ? 

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons notre futur(e) post-doctorant(e) en problèmes publics des centres de données pour rejoindre le département de recherche Sciences Économiques et Sociales (SES) et plus particulièrement la chaire SHS TerraAINs. 

Contexte scientifique : 

La Chaire SHS TerrAINs s’intéresse aux enjeux territoriaux du développement des infrastructures numériques et plus particulièrement des centres de données en France. Elle est portée par Pauline Gourlet et financée par la Région Ile de France (2026-2029).

Longtemps demeurés une infrastructure invisible, les centres de données ( data centers ) se trouvent désormais au cœur des problématiques des politiques publiques et industrielles et la Région Ile de France concentre aujourd’hui ces infrastructures (plus de 165 en 2024), avec de nombreux projets de data centers hyperscale à l’étude.

Vecteurs d’innovation, objets de spéculation, instruments de réaffirmation de puissance nationale, leur développement rapide génère aussi de nombreuses inquiétudes, voire du rejet, en France (comme à l’étranger), et ne fait pas à ce jour l’objet d’une planification concertée, mais relève encore largement d’opportunités isolées. Or, ces projets d’infrastructure se trouvent à la croisée d’enjeux locaux, voire hyper-locaux — de l’aménagement territorial aux effets sur l’environnement — et d’enjeux nationaux et internationaux — de la tension sur les réseaux d’électricité aux questions de souveraineté technologique et d’investissement.

Au sein de la Chaire, le ou la post-doctorant(e) étudiera la manière dont les centres de données, objets clés de l’infrastructure numérique, se développent et organisent différents problèmes publics relatifs aux « territoires » à différentes échelles territoriales. Comment en retour, la définition et la hiérarchisation de ces problèmes peuvent permettent des arbitrages concertés pour planifier leur déploiement ? 

Les modalités de participation à la construction de ces problèmes publics, autant que la fabrique des données nécessaires pour nourrir les positions des acteurs, sont autant un enjeu de démocratie technique qu’une manière de retrouver prise sur l’aménagement des milieux de vie. 

En articulant sociologie des sciences et des techniques et études urbaines avec une méthodologie innovante de recherche-action , TerrAINs contribue à rendre visibles et discutables les infrastructures numériques, tout en expérimentant des outils de représentation des problèmes et de participation, adaptées aux enjeux infrastructurels contemporains.

La Chaire est organisée selon trois axes principaux : 

- Analyse des discours sur les centres de données, et notamment les discours médiatiques régionaux, nationaux et étrangers ;

- Description des modalités du « faire infrastructure » : pratiques situées, relations aux milieux, frictions. Cet axe investira trois sites franciliens concernés par des projets de centres hyperscale.

- la chaire est conçue comme un laboratoire de recherche-action qui expérimente de nouvelles modalités de représentation et de participation autour des infrastructures numériques.

Vos missions principales seront de : 

- Assurer des missions de recherche dans le cadre de la Chaire Terrains

- Participer à l’animation de la chaire et contribuer aux projets menés par les autres membres de l’équipe

- Participer à des actions de valorisation des travaux menés au sein de la chaire

- Assurer des missions d’encadrement (stagiaires, workshops étudiant) 

Consulter la description des missions complètes dans la fiche de poste détaillée. 

Nous recherchons une personne avec un profil SHS – interdisciplinaire ( humanités environnementales, Science and Technology Studies (STS) ou anthropologie expérimentale, géographie sociale, architecture / design…) avec une solide maîtrise théorique et empirique des transformations socio-environnementales, des savoirs situés, des problèmes publics, de l’enquête collective et des relations entre sciences / société. 

Niveau de diplôme exigé : doctorat ou équivalent

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers). 

Vous bénéficierez de :

- 49 jours de congés annuels (CA + RTT)

- flexibilité des horaires de travail (en fonction de l'activité du service)

- télétravail 1 à 3 jours/semaine possible

- Remboursement abonnement transports en commun à 75%

- Proximité de nombreuses infrastructures sportives, conciergerie, parking souterrain, restauration interne...

- A savoir : nos cotisations sociales sont moins élevées que dans le secteur privé

Découvrez notre environnement de travail, nos engagements en image et en vidéo sur notre page dédiée . 

Dossier de candidature à envoyer avant le 20 novembre : 

- un CV détaillé

- une lettre (2-3 pages max) qui esquisse les contributions que le ou la candidat·e souhaiterait apporter au sein de la Chaire ainsi que sa motivation à y prendre part;

- deux publications significatives au regard de cette intention (au-delà des critères académiques classiques)

- une lettre de recommandation

Informations diverses : 

Date limite de candidature : 22 novembre 2026 

Type d'emploi : CDD de 18 mois 
Description de poste détaillée ici 
Rémunération : 36 000 euros brut/an

Nos recrutements sont fondés sur les compétences, sans distinction d’origine, d’âge, d'identité de genre et d’orientation sexuel et tous nos postes sont ouverts aux personnes en situation de handicap.

Dans le cadre d'un remplacement en interne, nous recrutons un·e Lead Data Engineer , basé·e à Lille.

Nous souhaitons accélérer la transformation et la digitalisation de nos processus RH, en partie grâce à une forte maîtrise de nos données People et de leurs usages. Pour accompagner cette transformation, nous déployons une plateforme RH mondiale (Workday) qui intégrera un CORE RH et plusieurs modules de talent management pour les 65 pays dans lesquels Decathlon est implanté.

Votre mission : Au croisement de la stratégie et de l'exécution technique, vous serez le/la garant·e technique de la migration de nos données depuis nos systèmes legacy vers Workday. En tant que Lead Data Engineer, vous concevrez l'architecture de transformation, piloterez la création des pipelines de données, et mettrez en place un monitoring rigoureux pour assurer une migration "zéro défaut". Vous travaillerez sous la responsabilité du Program Leader et en étroite collaboration avec les équipes projet locales et globales.

VOS RESPONSABILITÉS PRINCIPALES

1. Architecture et Stratégie de Transformation des données : 

- 
Définir l'architecture technique et la stratégie de migration des données de nos systèmes sources (legacies) vers le template cible Workday.

- 
Identifier le périmètre technique de la migration et concevoir des modèles de données répondant aux exigences fonctionnelles et de sécurité.

- 
Documenter de manière précise les systèmes sources, les flux, et les règles de transformation complexes.

2. Ingénierie et Développement (Hands-on & Leadership) : 

- 
Concevoir, développer et superviser des pipelines de données robustes, évolutifs et sécurisés (ETL) pour extraire, transformer et charger les données locales vers la plateforme mondiale.

- 
Définir et implémenter les règles de transformation avancées pour adapter nos données historiques aux standards stricts de l'intégrateur Workday.

- 
Assurer l'intégrité, le chiffrage et la sécurité des données RH (données sensibles) tout au long du processus.

title: People ops - M&A and International Expansion
description:
Health can’t wait . 

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

The M&A and International Expansion role 

Alan is diversifying its activities in the fields of healthcare, prevention and insurance through mergers and acquisitions, and is actively expanding internationally. In addition, Alan recruits talent worldwide and enables its employees to work remotely in complete safety.

“Alaner, everywhere”. The role makes sure each acquisition and each country opening is legally secure, fast and humane: from HR due diligence, to transferring employment contracts, to fully integrating the people who join us.

You'll join the Expansion crew inside the People team. You'll work closely with the crew owner, and with Corporate, Finance, team Leads and General Managers involved in each deal.

The People team 

The People team is made up of 13 people who work in an environment shaped by Alan's Leadership Principles. Every one of them is a genuine fan of our products (Culture being one of them) and deeply committed to Alan's Prevention and Health mission.

The team covers Learning and Development, Payroll and Admin, Employee Experience and Operational Efficiency, Compliance and Employment Law, Comp and Ben, and now M&A and International Expansion.

It is a generalist team: everyone shares three core missions, namely People on-call (answering the day to day questions from Alaners, which is now AI-powered), individual situation management, and HRBP responsibilities. This represents roughly 50% of our time. Then each person owns one or more cross-functional topics depending on their flavour. In your case: M&A and expansion.

Your missions 

On top of the core missions shared across the People team, you will work on a very diverse range of high-impact topics:

You will own to the People workstream of M&A transactions from due diligence to integration, alongside the crew and in close collaboration with the Corporate team, Legal, Finance and the business owners of each deal.

Depending on the nature of the deal, you will own:

- HR due diligence: reviewing headcount, employment contracts, collective agreements, compensation & benefits, liabilities and risks of target companies, and flagging red flags clearly to the deal team;

- Transferring employment contracts in France and abroad, and choosing the right path for each deal and country;

- Integrating acquired teams: day-1 and first-months plans, harmonising contracts and benefits, communicating with acquired employees, onboarding them into Alan's way of working;

- You will support the people transition of acquired teams, working with the crew and leads on team set-up, keeping key talents, and supporting every individual situation with care;

- Working with external advisors (law firms, HR advisory, relocation and EoR providers): writing clear briefs and challenging their advice.

Also:

- Opening new countries on the People side : entity vs employer of record, compliant local contracts, benefits and payroll partners

- You will handle international relocations and cross-border situations for Alaners moving or working between countries (visas, social security, tax, type of contract);

- Building reusable playbooks (HR due diligence checklist, integration playbook, "country opening – People" checklist) so each new deal is faster than the last

- Taking on global and cross-border individual situations (mobility, work from anywhere, sensitive cases)

- Raising the team's expertise : sharing your knowledge of employment law and M&A practices with the crew and the wider People team

- Leveraging AI and automation to multiply the impact of your work

Outcomes within your first months in the team 

By 2.5 months: 

- You are autonomous on day-to-day People on-call requests;

- You have mapped our current M&A and country-opening practices and shared a first list of gaps and quick wins;

- You have contributed to the People workstream of at least one live deal or country opening (due diligence, contract transfer or integration);

- You have contributed to our reusable playbook (e.g. HR due diligence checklist);

- You have shadowed and been reverse-shadowed on individual situation management.

By 5 months: 

- Depending on the ongoing projects, you own the People workstream of a deal end to end, from due diligence to integration, with the crew as a sounding board;

- You have run, or co-run, one talent density assessment and the parting ways cases that came with it;

- You handle cross-border individual situations without supervision;

- Your playbooks are used by the crew and by Legal / Finance on new deals;

- Leads and crew members come to you as the go-to expert on these topics.

Is this what you are looking for? 

You may be a great fit for this role if: 

- You have around 5 years of experience focused on HR M&A and integration topics, for example in a reputable HR advisory firm or in an HR team that focuses on these topics.

- You have worked on acquisitions in the Tech industry, not only on very large corporate groups, and you know the method is not the same.

- You master HR due diligence and the transfer of employment contracts.

- You have worked on post-merger integration, including talent density and parting ways, not only on the pre-signing side.

- You have international exposure: you have worked on deals or entities outside France.

- You are fluent in English, written and spoken (all of our internal processes, documentation and communications are in English).

- You are adaptable and creative: you adjust your method to each type of company and deal instead of copy-pasting one process.

- You are very organised: you run several confidential workstreams in parallel without dropping balls.

- You are a strong communicator, with very different audiences (founders, acquired employees, leads, lawyers), in writing and orally.

- You are strong technically and can teach us things.

- You show judgement and discretion with confidential information and sensitive human situations.

Nice-to-have 

We are not looking for all of the below. Any one of these can be a strong signal.

- You have a legal background, ideally in employment law.

- You have worked in or with a Tech scale-up that made several acquisitions.

- You have opened entities or set-up employers of record in new countries.

- You speak another language relevant to our expansion (e.g. Spanish, Portuguese; Arabic).

- You are AI-enthusiastic and actively use tools to multiply your impact.

Level range 

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the C0-D level range.

⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

Nice to have:
